title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Personal Annual Report. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Personal Annual Report
options.lineage: Swiss International Style annual reports and information design
options.thesis: Your spending, set as an annual report printed for an audience of one.
options.viewport: Red shell band with nav and Add; the month's spend as one huge figure, a proportional category bar, a 6-month column graphic, and a numbered entries table; a colophon reading 'Stored only in this browser'.
options.risk: Without the footnote drill-down and the colophon it falls back to a tidy, generic dashboard.

raised.raise: Every summary figure carries a footnote marker that opens the exact entries behind it, so no figure stands without its rows.
One-pixel rules and zero corner radius throughout; hierarchy comes from rules and type weight, not boxes and shadows.
Table columns are fixed and never reflow; filtered, new and pending-delete rows restyle in place.
One figure owns the dashboard; everything else steps back into small type and white space.
Amounts align on the decimal, tight to each column's right edge, in tabular figures.
On phones, adding an expense takes the whole screen as one focused sheet.

options.label: Envelope Security Tint
options.lineage: the tinted security patterns printed inside bank and tax envelopes
options.thesis: The pattern that hides your statement through the envelope becomes the app's privacy screen.
options.viewport: Navy shell rail; the dashboard sits in a white window cut into a tinted ground; a Privacy screen switch veils every amount in tint until you hover or focus it.
options.risk: The tint turns into wallpaper anywhere it isn't actually hiding something.

options.label: Monochrome Product Marketing
options.lineage: software marketing in one neutral scale
options.thesis: Near-black on near-white, one accent, every claim paired with proof.
options.risk: On a working screen it is the category default with fewer colours.
options.case: Fuses into a grey dashboard with one accent: clear, but it is the rut, and nothing in it says private.
options.kept: Claim and proof: every summary figure opens the entries behind it.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference Setting
options.thesis: Two dense columns around a vermilion rail of keys.
options.viewport: Two text columns twinned around a keyed centre rail.
options.risk: Reads as a book, and forms and tables fight the column measure.
options.case: Spending is not reading matter; the twin-column measure slows scanning amounts and dates.
options.kept: One-pixel rules, a limited set of values, no corner radius.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Rows as live entities on a board whose columns never move.
options.viewport: A board of expense rows flipping in character by character.
options.risk: A costume of a public signal on a private ledger.
options.case: Public broadcast is the opposite of private money; it identifies with travellers, not this audience.
options.kept: Fixed columns; state restyles a row without breaking the grid.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Names replaced by colour codes, one plot owning a black field.
options.viewport: One white-line plot on black, entries indexed by number.
options.risk: Coded labels make the reader decode every category.
options.case: Encoding hints at privacy, but it costs clarity on every row and drifts toward the dark look you ruled out.
options.kept: One figure owns the field; the rest steps back.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: Ballpoint lists timed to fill a side exactly.
options.viewport: A folded inlay with side A and side B listings.
options.risk: Playful by nature, which you ruled out.
options.case: Hand lettering and nostalgia undercut a serious money tool.
options.kept: Figures right-aligned tight against the margin.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the viewport, the next a snap away.
options.viewport: One expense per screen with a rail of glyphs.
options.risk: One item at a time defeats comparing and scanning.
options.case: An expense list needs side-by-side comparison; one-per-screen hides the totals.
options.kept: On phones, one focused task owns the whole screen.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern personal-finance dashboard, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar nav, four KPI cards, a trend chart and a transactions table.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every finance app by design.
